subject: Operationalizing no-training: certification, subprocessor attestations & onboarding artifacts
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Operationalizing no-training: certification, subprocessor attestations & onboarding artifacts

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for taking the time on the call this morning. As we discussed, Mediscope's priority is a contractual and operational assurance that customer-provided prompts and responses will not be used to improve or retrain models (no-training / no-derivative). To move from high-level language to something your procurement/legal team can accept, we want to provide both: 1) a narrow DPA addendum clause and 2) an operational attestation and supporting artifacts.

Quick ask: can you confirm the list of evidence your legal/procurement team requires for a no-training commitment? Based on similar customers, we typically provide:
- a signed Operational Statement on company letterhead (no-training attestation),
- current subprocessor inventory with access scope,
- KV/prefix logging retention policy and TTLs,
- representative export of audit logs showing role-based access controls, and
- contact for any additional security questionnaire fields.

If you can send the procurement checklist or any mandatory fields, we’ll assemble the artifacts and propose language that binds our runtime controls to the DPA clause. Proposed next steps:
- You send the procurement checklist / required evidence list by EOD Tue 6/15
- We prepare attachments + a one-page attestation and proposed DPA paragraph by Thu 6/18
- Quick 30-min legal ops call Fri 6/19 to walk through wording and execution

Attaching a short template of the Operational Statement we use for similar customers — happy to revise wording to match Mediscope's terms.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_no-train_operational_statement_v1.pdf (template)

From: Legal Ops <legal@mediscope.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@mediscope.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 12:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Operationalizing no-training: certification, subprocessor attestations & onboarding artifacts

Irene —

Thanks for the summary and the template. For procurement (and our security review) we need a clear mapping of contractual language to operational controls. At minimum our checklist requires: 
1) Signed attestation (company letterhead) explicitly stating "Redwood will not use Mediscope customer prompts/responses for model training or to create derivative models" and the date of the attestation.
2) Up-to-date subprocessor inventory with columns: subprocessor name, country, access level (read/write), purpose, and whether data residency guarantees apply.
3) KV/trace retention policy that includes default TTLs and whether prefixes are cached or persisted; indicate retention for prompt and response logs used for debugging.
4) Proof of key management (KMS) controls and onshore/offshore key locations if applicable.
5) An export of a recent access audit showing RBAC enforcement for the environment that will host our project.

Procurement attached our standard checklist for evidence and thresholds — please confirm which items Redwood can provide by next Thu 6/18. If there are any items you cannot provide, flag them and we will propose mitigations.

We prefer a combined approach: contractual DPA addendum + operational attestation. Also include a contact who can answer technical follow-ups.

Emma Torres
Senior Counsel, Mediscope Health
legal@mediscope.com

Attachment: mediscope_procurement_checklist.pdf

Team —

This is the right approach. A couple of drafting decisions for legal to consider so we don't over-promise but still give Mediscope comfort: 
- Contract language: "Redwood will not use Mediscope customer content for model training, improvement, or to create derivative models. Redwood's runtime logging for debugging and abuse detection will be limited and governed by the attached Operational Statement."
- Operational statement: include a statements section + a controls appendix that references the specific artifacts (subprocessor inventory, TTL policy, KMS location, audit export).
- Offer an "operational attestation" that is renewed annually or on major infra changes (helps procurement accept controls instead of continuous attestations).
- For prompt/response retention: propose 3 options in the attestation — 0 days (ephemeral), 3 days (diagnostic window), 30 days (special-case debugging) — and indicate default prod is 3 days unless customer opts into ephemeral API.

Also suggest we offer a limited-term addendum that includes a 3rd-party attestation option (SOC-type export) if Mediscope requires independent validation. If that’s required, mark as a procurement escalation to Marissa.

If we agree on the language, I’ll push a DPA addendum draft and the attestation template.

Jonas Weber
Principal Counsel, Redwood Inference
